answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by binding identity to physical co-presence at simultaneous pseudonymous parties. All meet at one instant; one body cannot be in two rooms at once, so one human earns one mark. A sybil behind a thousand clones must field a thousand people at once; a hollow roll of paper identities fills no seat. The scarce resource is a body's place and time, watched by attendees, so no clerk's quill pads the count. Like a lotus, one stem, one bloom. Cost grows linearly with humans, deterring cheap minting, not a wealthy recruiter; the tally trusts an honest counter.
